messages.text:
We propose replacing the adviser, copying and audit clauses with the following wording.

1. **Purpose and access.** The testing house may use the drawings and CAD files solely to prepare, perform and report the vibration tests specified in the test plan agreed by both parties. Access is limited to the test personnel identified by name and role in that plan. Before gaining access, each person must be bound in writing by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as this agreement. An adviser, subcontractor or substitute requires the design owner’s prior written approval by name and role. Email approval is sufficient. The testing house remains responsible for each approved person’s compliance.

2. **Working copies and fixtures.** The testing house may make the working copies reasonably necessary for the agreed tests, provided it encrypts them in transit and at rest and limits access to approved personnel. It may extract only the geometry needed to design and fabricate fixtures for those tests. The same access and use restrictions apply to fixture files and physical fixtures. The testing house must neither use nor allow others to use the drawings, CAD geometry or derivatives to develop a competing product.

3. **Destruction and verification.** Within 30 calendar days after the design owner accepts the test report in writing, or after earlier termination of the work, the testing house must securely erase the supplied files and all working and derivative files, destroy physical copies and derivative fixtures, and obtain confirmation of destruction from any approved external recipient. Within that same period, it must give the design owner a signed certificate identifying the material destroyed by category, the method and date of destruction, and any outstanding exceptions. The testing house may retain a test report containing results and observations that do not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry.

We would accept certification by an independent verifier bound to confidentiality in place of on-demand site access. The verifier could inspect deletion records and fixture disposal evidence without receiving the CAD files. Can your backup system meet the 30-day deadline? If it requires a longer period, please propose a maximum expiry period for isolated backup copies and a way to certify their final deletion.

The framework is workable, subject to the following amendments. I can meet the 30-day deadline for active systems, but isolated backup copies require a maximum 90-day expiry period.

### 1. Approved personnel, external specialists and substitution

Replace the access-approval provisions in clause 1 with:

> Personnel and external recipients must be identified by name, role, organisation and permitted scope of access in the agreed test plan or in **Attachment 1—Approved Access Schedule**. The approved machining shop may receive only the isolated drawing extracts necessary to design and fabricate the test fixtures. The accredited laboratory may receive only the material necessary to perform and document the agreed tests. Neither external recipient may disclose the material to another person or organisation.
>
> The testing house may propose a replacement specialist or other substitute by email, identifying the person’s name, role, organisation and scope of access. The design owner’s approval must not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, and the design owner will respond within two business days. Email approval is sufficient. No substitute may receive access before approval, and the testing house may suspend the affected work while approval is pending. Attachment 1 must be updated to reflect each approved change. The testing house remains responsible for approved external recipients’ compliance.

This gives us a workable substitution process without treating the machining shop or laboratory as unrestricted advisers.

### 2. Copies, extracts and fixtures

Add to clause 2:

> Each drawing extract must be separately identified and access-controlled, and must contain only the geometry reasonably required for the relevant fixture or test activity. The testing house must maintain a record of the extracts and working copies supplied to each approved external recipient. These records may exclude the underlying geometry.
>
> Required calibration and test-equipment records are not working or derivative files merely because they identify the equipment, methods, dates, environmental conditions or test results used.

### 3. Destruction, backups and retained records

Replace clause 3 with:

> Within 30 calendar days after written acceptance of the test report, or earlier termination of the work, the testing house must securely erase the supplied files and all working and derivative files on active systems, destroy physical copies and derivative fixtures, and obtain equivalent destruction confirmation from each approved external recipient.
>
> Copies contained solely in encrypted, isolated backup systems may remain until their scheduled deletion, which must occur no later than 90 calendar days after the same triggering event. Those copies must not be accessed or used except where restoration is necessary for disaster recovery. Following any restoration, the relevant material must be re-deleted without restarting the 90-day period and must not be used for testing or any other purpose.
>
> Within the initial 30-day period, the testing house must provide a signed certificate identifying the material destroyed by category, the method and date of destruction, and any backup copies still awaiting scheduled deletion. Within five business days after final backup deletion, it must provide a supplementary certificate confirming completion. **Attachment 2—Destruction Certificate** will include fields for active systems, external recipients, physical fixtures, backup expiry and final deletion.
>
> The testing house may retain: (a) the test report, provided it does not disclose or permit reconstruction of the CAD geometry; and (b) for at least two years, calibration records, equipment records, test-method records, approvals, access logs, destruction confirmations and verification certificates required for accreditation, quality control or demonstrating compliance. Such retained records must not contain drawing extracts, CAD geometry or information permitting its reconstruction, and must remain subject to the confidentiality obligations.

### 4. Verification in place of site-access rights

The independent-verifier proposal should replace the audit clause entirely:

> At the design owner’s request, an independent verifier jointly selected by the parties and bound by written confidentiality obligations may verify compliance with the destruction and fixture-disposal obligations. Verification will ordinarily be conducted through review of deletion logs, backup-expiry records, destruction certificates, external-recipient confirmations and fixture-disposal evidence, without disclosure of CAD files or geometry to the verifier.
>
> If a premises visit is reasonably necessary, it requires at least ten business days’ notice, must occur during normal business hours, and is limited to premises controlled by the testing house. There will be no unannounced inspection and no inspection of a shared customer site or an external recipient’s premises. Evidence from the machining shop or accredited laboratory will instead be supplied through their destruction confirmations or other records that do not expose third-party information.
>
> The verifier’s report must be limited to whether the specified destruction and retention obligations have been met and must protect other customers’ information. The design owner bears the verifier’s costs unless the verifier identifies a material breach, in which case the testing house bears the reasonable verification costs.

These amendments preserve meaningful verification while accommodating the required external specialists, two-year geometry-free record retention and controlled backup expiry.

We accept the proposed amendments, including the two-business-day response period for substitutions, the 90-day backup deadline, retention of geometry-free quality records and independent verification on the notice, scope and cost terms in clause 4.

Please include the following wording in clause 1 to carry forward the confidentiality requirement for everyone who handles the material.

> Access is limited to individuals listed by name, role, organisation and permitted scope in the agreed test plan or Attachment 1. Before disclosure, the testing house must ensure that each listed individual and each approved external organisation is bound in writing by confidentiality and use restrictions at least as protective as those in this agreement. Approval of an organisation authorises access only by its listed individuals. The testing house remains responsible for compliance by its personnel and approved external recipients.

Please also add the following sentence to clause 3 so that Attachment 2 accounts for copies held by the machining shop and laboratory.

> The same destruction deadlines and backup restrictions apply to each approved external recipient. The testing house must identify any recipient backups in its initial certificate and obtain written confirmation of their final deletion in time to include that confirmation in its supplementary certificate.

With those clarifications, we agree to the replacement terms. The agreed-test-only purpose, encryption requirements and prohibition on using the materials or derivatives to develop competing products remain part of clauses 1 and 2.

One practical fixture issue should be covered in the sign-off terms. The approved machining shop already has stock cut for the original fixture. I can avoid both unnecessary scrapping and any broader drawing disclosure by adding the following as **Attachment 3—Fixture Control and Test Sign-off**.

### 1. Custody of stock, coupon and tolerance information

> The existing cut stock must remain segregated at the approved machining shop under a unique fixture or batch identifier. It may be completed or reworked solely for the original fixture, must not be used for other work, and must not be transferred to another organisation. The testing house must record its quantity, location and eventual use or disposal.
>
> The reference coupon must remain in locked, access-controlled custody at the testing house. Only the approved test lead and other specifically authorised personnel may handle it. It must not be sent to the machining shop or laboratory. It must be returned to the design owner on request or otherwise handled in accordance with clause 3.
>
> The machining shop may receive only the tolerance table necessary to complete or verify the fixture. It will not receive the coupon, raw measurement files or any additional CAD material. The tolerance table is controlled derivative material subject to the existing access, transmission and destruction requirements.

If the fixture is rejected, the affected stock and fixture must remain quarantined pending approved rework or disposal, with disposal evidenced under the agreed certification process.

### 2. Measurement and repeatability check

> Before further machining, the design owner must provide the applicable datums, dimensional tolerances and acceptance criteria in writing and approve the repeatability-check procedure. The testing house’s test lead will measure the reference coupon at the testing house using calibrated equipment. Unless another procedure is agreed, the check will comprise three independent repeated measurements.
>
> The testing house will provide the design owner with the proposed tolerance table and a summary identifying the equipment and calibration status, measurement spread or uncertainty, and whether the agreed repeatability criterion was met. The design owner must approve the tolerance table and repeatability outcome by email before the table is released to the machining shop.

The retained quality record may identify the table by version and record calibration, repeatability performance and pass/fail status, but need not retain the dimensional table or raw geometry-bearing measurements after the applicable destruction deadline.

### 3. Fixture and test sign-off

> The machining shop must confirm in writing that the completed fixture conforms to the approved tolerance table. The testing house must verify the fixture and test setup against the agreed acceptance criteria and submit a test-readiness statement to the design owner. Vibration testing must not begin until the design owner gives written test-readiness approval by email. Any deviation requires rework and renewed approval or the design owner’s written concession.

For final sign-off, I propose that the design owner accept the test report or identify specific deficiencies within five business days after submission. If it does neither, the report should be deemed accepted **solely for starting the clause 3 destruction period**, without preventing correction of a subsequently identified reporting error.

### 4. Two-business-day reviews and resulting delay

> The design owner will respond within two business days to the tolerance/repeatability submission and to the test-readiness submission. Where a related substitution approval is also required, the reviews will run concurrently rather than consecutively, although neither access nor testing may begin before the applicable express approval.
>
> The testing house may suspend the affected work while awaiting a response and will not be in delay for that suspension. Affected milestones will move by the actual period of suspension, without double counting overlapping reviews. Each party bears its own costs where the design owner responds within the two-business-day period. For a later response, the testing house is entitled to a day-for-day extension and reimbursement of reasonable, documented external standby or rebooking costs, provided it notifies the design owner promptly of those costs.

This allows the existing stock to be used under controlled custody, but keeps further machining and testing dependent on your tolerance specification, acceptance of the repeatability check and express test-readiness sign-off.

We propose adding the following terms to Attachment 3 for this prototype batch. Only the geometry on page 4 of the actuator drawing is export-restricted. We can prepare an alternative reference coupon in two days once we agree on the verification test. In the meantime, the machining shop may keep the cut stock segregated under its batch identifier, and work independent of that geometry may continue.

> **Controlled release.** The design owner will supply a drawing set from which the page 4 geometry has been removed, including from any embedded CAD data. The testing house, machining shop and laboratory may receive only owner-cleared material within their respective approved scopes. The original coupon and any extract, dimensions, measurements or combination of records from which the restricted geometry can be reconstructed must be withheld. If any recipient already holds such material, it must immediately suspend access and use, secure the material in place and notify the design owner by identifier without forwarding it.
>
> **Alternative coupon and verification.** Before coupon preparation begins, the parties will agree by email on the fixture characteristics the alternative coupon must verify, the applicable datums, the permitted deviation from the owner’s reference values and the maximum repeatability spread. The design owner will prepare the cleared coupon within two days of that agreement. At the testing house, the approved test lead will independently remove, reseat and measure the coupon three times using calibrated equipment. Each reading must meet the agreed dimensional limits, and the spread must meet the agreed repeatability limit. The test lead will submit the results and calibration details to the design owner. If the coupon cannot verify a required fixture characteristic, affected machining stays on hold until the parties agree on a revised check.
>
> **Stock and release gates.** The design owner must confirm in writing that the existing stock is suitable for the cleared fixture work and approve both the verification result and the exact version of the tolerance table before machining resumes. The shop may receive only that approved table. The alternative coupon stays in controlled custody at the testing house until return or destruction. Vibration testing requires separate express test-readiness approval.

We accept the concurrent two-business-day reviews and a milestone extension for the actual suspension, counted once. The two days for coupon preparation are a planned milestone. For a review response beyond the agreed window, we accept reasonable, documented external standby or rebooking costs that the testing house promptly flags and takes reasonable steps to minimise.

We also accept the five-business-day report review. If we neither accept the report nor identify specific deficiencies within that period, the clause 3 destruction clock starts at the end of the fifth business day. That trigger applies solely to destruction and preserves the obligation to correct reporting errors.

Please confirm whether any recipient already holds page 4 geometry or stock embodying it, using identifiers only. Please also identify the fixture characteristics your test lead needs the alternative coupon to verify so we can agree the limits and start the two-day preparation period.

We accept Attachment 3 and the related scheduling, cost and report-review provisions, subject to the record-handling clarification below.

### Recipient and stock confirmation

Using **TH-01** for the testing house, **MS-01** for the machining shop, **AL-01** for the accredited laboratory and **STK-01** for the segregated stock batch:

- Neither TH-01, MS-01 nor AL-01 holds page 4 geometry, the original coupon, a restricted extract, or measurements intended to reproduce that geometry.
- MS-01 holds STK-01 as unmachined cut stock, segregated under that batch identifier. STK-01 does not embody page 4 geometry, and no restricted fixture features have been machined into it.
- AL-01 holds no coupon, drawing geometry or stock requiring suspension.
- Accordingly, no additional controlled material currently needs to be secured in place or notified under the controlled-release paragraph.

### Alternative-coupon verification proposal

We propose the following verification schedule. Datum locations and owner-cleared reference values should be supplied in a separately versioned verification instruction, using characteristic and check-point identifiers without reproducing restricted nominal geometry.

| ID | Fixture characteristic to verify | Datum scheme | Proposed dimensional limit for each reading | Maximum spread across three readings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| VC-01 | Primary seating location normal to the seating plane, measured at the agreed seating check points | Primary datum A | Reference value ±0.05 mm | 0.02 mm at each check point |
| VC-02 | Secondary locating-interface position in the seating plane | Datums A and B | Reference value ±0.05 mm | 0.02 mm |
| VC-03 | Tertiary clocking/anti-rotation location, measured as linear displacement at the agreed check point | Datums A, B and C | Reference value ±0.05 mm | 0.02 mm |
| VC-04 | Full seating and ability to apply the cleared restraint arrangement without forcing the coupon or preventing correct seating | A, B and C, as applicable | Pass on each removal/reseating cycle; any rocking, interference or forced seating is a failure | Not applicable |

The three measurement cycles will be fully independent removal, reseating and measurement cycles. Measurement equipment will have resolution of 0.005 mm or better and calibration valid throughout the verification. Results will be recorded as deviations from the owner-cleared reference values. Calibration details will be limited to equipment and calibration-certificate identifiers, calibration dates and due dates, and other geometry-free quality information.

Please confirm these characteristics and limits and provide the cleared datum map and reference values by email. That exchange will constitute the agreement starting the two-day coupon-preparation period. If any characteristic requires a different limit for fixture function, please identify it by VC identifier and supply the revised limit.

### Records and release documentation

Add to Attachment 3:

> Verification results, the approved verification instruction and calibration details may be retained under clause 3 only to the extent they are owner-cleared as not disclosing or permitting reconstruction of restricted geometry, whether individually or in combination. Verification records will use characteristic and check-point identifiers and deviations from cleared reference values rather than restricted nominal dimensions. Return or destruction of the alternative coupon will be recorded by coupon identifier in the Attachment 2 certification process.

The stock-suitability, verification-result and tolerance-table reviews may run concurrently once their respective submission packages are complete. Release of one item does not imply release of another, and none of those approvals constitutes vibration test-readiness approval.

We also agree that correction of a reporting error does not itself restart the destruction clock, unless the parties agree that additional controlled material must be supplied for the correction. The five-business-day report-review mechanism otherwise applies exactly as proposed.

We accept the VC-01 through VC-04 verification schedule. For VC-01 through VC-03, each reading must be within ±0.05 mm of its cleared reference value, and the spread across the three independent removal and reseating cycles must be no more than 0.02 mm at each applicable check point. VC-04 must pass on every cycle. We accept the proposed equipment resolution of 0.005 mm or better and the requirement for calibration to remain valid throughout verification.

The remaining deliverable is the cleared datum map and reference values. The design owner will issue them to the approved TH-01 test lead by email in a versioned verification instruction. That email will start the two-day coupon-preparation period. MS-01 may receive only the separately approved tolerance table.

We accept your records wording with one clarification to preserve the clause 3 retention limit. Please replace “restricted geometry” in the first sentence with “any actuator CAD geometry.” Owner clearance must cover the retained records both individually and in combination. We agree to record coupon return or destruction by identifier in Attachment 2.

We accept the custody confirmations. STK-01 may remain segregated pending express written stock-suitability approval. The stock, verification-result and tolerance-table reviews may run concurrently, and all three approvals are required before machining resumes. Vibration testing requires its own express readiness approval. We also accept the report-correction wording.

The records provision will read:

> No retained record may contain any actuator CAD geometry, and no retained record or combination of records may disclose or permit reconstruction of that geometry. The design owner must clear the retained records both individually and in combination. Subject to that clearance, the testing house may retain the test report and the calibration, equipment, test-method, approval, access, destruction and verification records specified in clause 3 for at least two years.

The two-day coupon-preparation period will start only upon TH-01’s receipt of the versioned verification instruction containing the cleared datum map and reference values. MS-01’s access remains limited to the separately approved tolerance table. That instruction will not itself authorise machining resumption or vibration testing: the three specified approvals remain prerequisites to machining, and vibration testing still requires its own express readiness approval.

Attachment 2 will record each coupon’s return or destruction by identifier, without including actuator CAD geometry.
